title: Benchmark Designers Should “Train on the Test Set” to Expose Exploitable Non-Visual Shortcuts

bias_targets.methodology: Applying a 'Test-set Stress-Test' (TsT) using k-fold cross-validation to train blind diagnostic models (an LLM via LoRA and a Random Forest) exclusively on the textual, non-visual inputs of multimodal test sets to derive a quantitative exploitability measure and sample-level bias scores.

Analyzing hand-crafted non-visual features (such as answer distribution skews, predictable object sizes, and target-position correlations) using a Random Forest classifier to extract feature importance (Gini importance) and identify spurious correlations embedded in benchmark structures.

Evaluating zero-shot and fine-tuned 'blind' (vision-disabled) language models on multimodal questions to quantify the extent to which world knowledge acquired during LLM pretraining allows models to bypass visual reasoning.
